rationales: Carbon (spelled “Carban” here) is a major bio-element, but it is not the most abundant in protoplasm.
Hydrogen is abundant in protoplasm, but its percentage is lower than oxygen’s.
Oxygen is the most abundant major bio-element in protoplasm.
Nitrogen is an important bio-element, but it is not present in the highest percentage.
A population is a group of organisms of the same species living in an area.
The biosphere is the part of Earth inhabited by living organisms.
A species is a group of similar organisms, not the whole inhabited part of Earth.
Co-ordination is the integration of activities, not a region inhabited by organisms.
A hypothesis is a tentative explanation formed after initial observations.
Deduction is reasoning from a hypothesis to testable predictions, not the basic first step.
Experiments test predictions and are not the basic first step.
Observation is the basic initial step of the biological method.
Allium cepa is the scientific name of onion.
“Zia-maize” is not the scientific name of starfish.
Asterias rubens is a scientific name for a starfish.
Carvus splendens is not the scientific name of starfish.
Chitin is found in fungal cell walls and arthropod exoskeletons, not typical plant cell walls.
Lignin occurs in some plant cell walls but is not their general structural material.
Cellulose is the main structural component of plant cell walls.
Plasmodes are channels between plant cells, not a cell-wall chemical.
Germ cells give rise to reproductive cells rather than forming the general body tissues.
Gametes are reproductive cells, not the cells that form the body.
Somatic cells form the body of an organism.
Parent cells are cells that produce other cells, not the specific term for body cells.
Lipase breaks down fats, not starch.
Protease breaks down proteins, not starch.
Amylase breaks down starch.
Pepsin is a protein-digesting enzyme in the stomach.
Glycolysis takes place in the cytoplasm.
The nucleus is not the site of glycolysis.
Mitochondria carry out later stages of cellular respiration, not glycolysis.
Chloroplasts carry out photosynthesis, not glycolysis.
Pepsinogen is activated into pepsin in the stomach.
Bicarbonate does not result from the conversion of pepsinogen.
Hydrochloric acid helps activate pepsinogen but is not its product.
Gastrin is a hormone that regulates gastric activity, not the product of pepsinogen activation.
Glucose is commonly converted into sucrose for transport in most plants.
Sucrose is the main form in which food is transported in most plants.
Starch is mainly a storage carbohydrate and is insoluble for transport.
Protein is not the usual transported form of food in plants.
The left atrium has thinner walls than the ventricles.
The right atrium has thinner walls than the ventricles.
The left ventricle has the thickest wall because it pumps blood throughout the body.
The right ventricle pumps blood to the lungs and has a thinner wall than the left ventricle.
Biology is the broad study of living organisms, not specifically animals.
Zoology is the scientific study of animals.
Botany is the study of plants.
Microbiology is the study of microorganisms.
Jabir Bin Hayan is associated with early chemistry, not authorship of this medical work.
Abdul Malik Asmai was a scholar of zoology and related subjects, not the author of this book.
Bu Ali Sina (Avicenna) wrote Al-Qanun-fil-Tib.
Robert Brown was a botanist known for describing the cell nucleus.
A hypothesis that withstands repeated testing and remains supported may be developed into a theory.
A law describes a consistent natural relationship and is not simply a hypothesis that has survived testing.
A principle is a general foundational rule, not the usual term for a repeatedly supported hypothesis.
A deduction is a logical prediction drawn from a hypothesis or other premise.
The family name is not the first word in a binomial scientific name.
The class name is not part of the two-word binomial name.
The first letter of the genus name is capitalized.
The species name begins with a lowercase letter.
